app.name: Mirkomil Host
admin.title: Administrative access
admin.on: Administrative access is on: the panel can manage the system (services, updates, reboot). Such actions carry an "admin" badge and are written to the activity log.
admin.off: You are in limited mode: view only. Turn on administrative access to manage the system.
simple.ok.title: All good
simple.footer: Dangerous actions (reboot, delete) always ask for confirmation and are logged.
page.soon.body: This page arrives in the next milestone ({m}).
error.title: Something went wrong in this section
error.body: The rest of the panel still works. Retry, or copy the details.
terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.note: This is Cockpit's own terminal — it runs as the logged-in user.
settings.title: Settings
guardian.title: Guardian
guardian.unavailable: The Guardian agent is not running or not installed.
guardian.unavailable.hint: Run on the server: sudo mirkomil repair
chart.needsGuardian: 24h / 7d history comes from the Guardian agent
guardian.mode.dryrun.help: Guardian only records what it would do and changes nothing. Watch the timeline for a few days, then switch to Automatic.
guardian.mode.auto.help: Guardian fixes problems itself and records them in the timeline and Telegram.
guardian.adminOnly: Only an administrator can change this
chart.net.note: Network — relative to the peak in range
quick.title: Quick actions
projects.title: Active projects
projects.empty.title: No projects yet
projects.empty.body: Deploy a GitHub project in a few clicks — coming in the next milestone (M5).
projects.col.name: Project
activity.title: Recent activity
alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.noAgent: Guardian agent not running — alerts unavailable
admin.intro: Enter your password for system actions (services, updates, reboot). It goes straight to the system (sudo) and is never stored.
admin.failed: Could not turn on administrative access
admin.noBridge: This user has no sudo rights.
action.needAdmin: Turn on administrative access (shield button at the top)
services.title: Services
svc.confirm.stop: “{unit}” will be stopped. Anything depending on it may stop working.
svc.confirm.restart: “{unit}” will be restarted. Expect a few seconds of downtime.
svc.confirm.disable: “{unit}” will no longer start on boot.
power.title: Power
power.intro: Reboot or shut down the server. Both require typing the server name and are logged.
power.reboot.body: The server restarts. Bots and apps stop for 1–2 minutes, then start again.
power.shutdown.body: The server powers off completely. You will need physical access to turn it back on!
power.sent: Command sent. The connection will drop — refresh in a minute or two.
updates.title: Updates
updates.reboot.body: The new kernel or libraries take effect after a reboot.
updates.confirm: {n} packages will be upgraded. This can take a few minutes; some services restart briefly.
updates.auto: Security updates install automatically every day (unattended-upgrades).
logs.title: Logs
logs.journalNote: The full system journal needs the “adm” group or administrative access.
activityPage.title: Activity log
activityPage.intro: Important actions done through the panel (who, what, target, result) and Guardian's automatic actions.
activityPage.empty: No actions through the panel yet
sec.title: Security
sec.needAdmin: Turn on administrative access for the full check — only root can read the firewall, fail2ban and SSH settings.
sec.firewall.on: On — incoming connections denied by default
sec.unban.confirm: {ip} will be unbanned and may try to connect again.
sec.rec.ufw: Enable the firewall: sudo mirkomil repair
sec.rec.f2b: Start fail2ban: sudo systemctl enable --now fail2ban
sec.rec.password: Add an SSH key and disable password login (sudo mirkomil repair)
sec.rec.none: Everything is configured well — no recommendations
identity.title: Server identity
identity.intro: The name and domain are used on the login page, panel, browser title and Telegram alerts. Changing them updates everything.
identity.name: Server / hosting name
identity.saved: Saved. The login page updates — you will need to log in again in about 10 seconds.
identity.adminOnly: Only an administrator can change this
deploy.title: Deploy / Projects
deploy.intro: Deploy a GitHub project in a few clicks: the type is detected automatically and it runs in a hardened container.
deploy.empty.title: No projects yet
deploy.empty.body: Paste a GitHub URL — the panel clones, builds, health-checks and runs it.
deploy.domainNote: Public access is enabled in M6 (Cloudflare Tunnel)
wizard.title: New project
wizard.name: Project name
wizard.envHint: Secrets are stored root-only on the server and are never shown again.
wizard.invalidName: 3–32 chars: lowercase letters, digits and '-', starting with a letter
app.rollback.confirm: The app rolls back to {id} (the old image is started again).
app.delete.body: “{name}” is removed completely: containers, images, code and env. This cannot be undone.
app.settings.saved: Saved. Applied on the next deploy.
app.notDeployed: The app has not been deployed successfully yet.
docker.title: Docker
docker.intro: All containers on the server. Mirkomil apps start with “mk-”.
docker.prune.body: Unused images and build cache are removed. Volumes (data) and running containers are not touched.
docker.adminOnly: The Docker page is for administrators only.
docker.col.name: Name
db.title: Databases
db.intro: PostgreSQL and Redis in one click. Passwords are generated and stay on the server; databases are not reachable from outside.
db.name: Database name
db.empty.title: No databases yet
db.empty.body: Create PostgreSQL (for Django, FastAPI) or Redis (cache, queues, bot state) and attach it to a project.
db.attached: Attached to {app} as {var}. Redeploy to apply.
db.delete.body: The “{name}” container is removed. Data (volume) is KEPT by default.
db.dropData: Also delete the data (cannot be undone)
auto.title: Auto-deploy
auto.help: Guardian checks the branch every 5 minutes and deploys new commits itself. A broken commit is not retried.
key.title: Private repo (deploy key)
key.help: For a private repo use git@github.com:owner/repo.git and add this public key in GitHub → Settings → Deploy keys (read-only). The private key never leaves the server.
wizard.repoHintPrivate: Private: git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>.git — then add the deploy key in Settings
dom.intro: Your server goes online without open ports: the panel sits behind Cloudflare Access, each app gets its own subdomain, SSL is automatic.
dom.mismatch: The tunnel is set up for {old} but the server domain is {now}. Reconnect from Settings.
dom.noPorts: The server only connects outward — no router ports to open.
dom.panelHint: Only these emails can sign in (Google, GitHub or an email code). Sessions last 7 days; the server password is still required.
dom.noHosts: No web apps yet. Once you deploy, the address appears here automatically.
dom.custom: For your own domain (e.g. shop.uz) add a CNAME pointing to the app address.
dom.setup.title: 4 steps to connect
dom.step1: Add {domain} to Cloudflare (free plan) and switch its nameservers at your registrar.
dom.step2: Open dash.cloudflare.com → Zero Trust once and pick the free plan (choose a team name).
dom.step3: In Cloudflare: Manage Account → Account API Tokens → Create Token → “Custom token” (or My Profile → API Tokens) — with exactly these permissions:
dom.step4: Paste the token and the emails allowed into the panel — the server does the rest.
dom.tokenKeep: leave empty to keep the stored token
dom.tokenHint: Both new “cfat_…” account tokens and user tokens work. Stored on the server only (root), never shown again.
dom.emailsHint: Comma separated. They sign in with Google/GitHub or an emailed code.
net.intro: How the server can be reached. No port is open to the internet.
net.cfOff: Not set up — connect it in Domains & SSL
net.why1: No router ports: the tunnel only connects outward, so attackers can't reach your IP directly.
net.why2: The panel has two layers: Cloudflare Access and the server password; cloudflared also verifies the Access signature.
net.why3: Databases, Docker and internal services are never published.
fm.intro: Server files, with your own permissions. Drag & drop to upload, double-click to open.
fm.adminHint: Work as root (every action is logged)
fm.adminNote: Admin mode: actions run as root. Be careful with system files.
fm.binary: This isn't a text file, so it can't be edited. You can download it.
fm.conflict: The file changed on the server after you opened it. Reopen it and reapply your edits.
fm.deleteAdmin: Admin mode: deleting as root, without restrictions.
fm.deleteBody: {n} item(s) will be deleted permanently (there is no trash):
fm.discard: You have unsaved changes. Close anyway?
fm.emptyHint: Drag files here or press Upload.
fm.extractBody: “{name}” will be extracted into {dir}. Existing files are not overwritten.
fm.name: Name
fm.noMatch: No match here — press Enter to search subfolders
fm.overwriteBody: These files already exist. Replace them? (Cancel uploads only the new ones)
role.admin.about: Everything: users, domains, security, Docker. But not sudo.
role.developer.about: Deploys own projects; logs, files, terminal, databases.
role.noAccess: Your role can't open this section. Ask an administrator.
users.intro: Who can sign in and what they can do. Each user is a separate Linux account.
users.badLogin: 2–31 chars, starting with a lowercase letter (a-z, 0-9, _ -)
users.appsHint: Developers and viewers only see these projects (and ones they created).
users.groupsHint: Safe groups only. Root-equivalent groups like sudo or docker can't be granted here.
users.emailHint: If a domain is connected, this email is allowed to reach the panel from the internet.
users.ownerHint: In the sudo group — not changed from the panel
users.deleteBody: The “{user}” account will be deleted and signed out. Its home folder is kept.
invite.title: Invite card
invite.text.title: Panel sign-in details
invite.text.first: You'll set your own password at first sign-in.
invite.once: This password is shown only now and isn't stored anywhere. Copy or print it.
invite.access: {email} was allowed to reach the panel from the internet.
account.title: My account
account.pwHint: This is your Linux password: panel sign-in and admin mode.
account.err.weak: New password is too weak — choose a longer, less common one
account.rememberOff: Now: your Linux password is asked every time you switch to admin mode (safer).
account.rememberOn: Now: admin mode turns on automatically when you sign in (reuses your login password).
site.title: Publish as a site
site.required: {type} is built for websites, so it's always published.
site.bot: A bot (e.g. aiogram) isn't a site by default — it runs privately. Turn on if it needs a webhook.
site.optional: Optional: when on, it's served at <app>.<domain>.
site.portHint: When on, the app must listen for HTTP on the port in $PORT.
site.autoHint: Auto: decided from the code — webhook or web server → site, polling bot → private.
site.saved: Saved — applies on the next deploy
env.intro: Click the pencil next to a key to change its value. Values are visible only to people with access to this project, and every viewing is logged.
env.pending: Changes take effect when the app restarts.
env.applying: Restarting the app with the new env…
env.err.bad: Key: letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit
env.err.port: PORT is set by the server
env.err.exists: This key exists — edit it with the pencil
update.ready: A new panel version was installed. Sign in again to use it.
hook.title: GitHub webhook (push → deploy)
hook.intro: Every push to “{branch}” starts a deploy right away — no 5-minute wait.
hook.enabled: Webhook on — add the secret on GitHub
hook.needDomain: GitHub needs a connected domain (Cloudflare Tunnel) to reach the server. Until then auto-deploy checks every 5 minutes.
hook.step1: On GitHub: repo → Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook:
hook.step2: Paste the Payload URL, Content type (application/json) and Secret from above.
hook.step3: Choose “Just the push event” and save. GitHub sends a ping — “Connected” appears below.
hook.rotated: New secret — update it on GitHub too
wizard.rootDirAuto: auto — repo root or the only project folder
wizard.rootDirHint: If the project lives in a subfolder (e.g. bot or apps/web). Leave empty to find it automatically.
dom.who.everyone.about: Any email receives a code, then the server login follows; the role decides what each person sees.
dom.who.emails.about: Safest: anyone else never even sees the server login page.
dom.panelHintEveryone: Any email gets a login code (7-day session), then the server login and password; the role decides access.
